title: All Subsets of a Set of Letters

concept.title: Choose, explore, unchoose
body: A set of `n` letters has `2^n` subsets. To list them all, build every subset one letter at a time. Keep the subset built so far in a list `current`. At each step the next letter must come **after** the last chosen one (this avoids listing the same subset in two different orders), so the function receives the position `start` where the next letter may be taken from.

The three lines **choose - explore - unchoose** are the heart of **backtracking**. After the exploration the list `current` must be exactly as before the choice, otherwise the next iteration would start from a wrong state. Because the letters are given in alphabetical order, the subsets come out in dictionary order: `a`, `ab`, `abc`, `ac`, `b`, `bc`, `c`.

statement: You are given `n` different lowercase letters in alphabetical order. Print all non-empty subsets of the letters. Inside a subset the letters keep their alphabetical order. Print the subsets in dictionary order, one per line.
inputFormat: The only line has the letters as one word.
outputFormat: The `2^n - 1` non-empty subsets in dictionary order, one per line.
constraints: The letters are different and in alphabetical order.

examples.output:
a
ab
abc
ac
b
bc
c
examples.note: The 7 subsets in dictionary order are a, ab, abc, ac, b, bc, c.

hints: Build each subset in a list: add a letter, record the subset, recurse, then remove the letter again.
After a letter at position i, only letters at positions i + 1 and later may be added.
Recording the subset before going deeper gives the dictionary order: a shorter subset comes before the longer ones that start with it.

explanation: Every call tries each letter from `start` on: it adds the letter, records the subset, explores the subsets that extend it, and removes the letter. Each non-empty subset is recorded exactly once, in dictionary order.
solution.complexity: Time O(2^n * n), space O(n) besides the output.

code.python:
def subsets(word, start, current, out):
    for i in range(start, len(word)):
        current.append(word[i])
        out.append("".join(current))
        subsets(word, i + 1, current, out)
        current.pop()

word = input().strip()

out = []
subsets(word, 0, [], out)
print("\n".join(out))
